html:
An Arab navigator born around 1432 in Julfar, in today's United Arab Emirates, from a family of sailors. He wrote the most detailed guides to sailing the Indian Ocean that survive from before European ships arrived.

His best known book, the Kitab al-Fawa'id, sets out the stars used to find a ship's position, the monsoon seasons, coasts, reefs and routes from the Red Sea and the Gulf to East Africa, India and beyond. He also wrote many navigation poems, which made the rules easy to remember. Together they show the skill behind the Indian Ocean trade of his day.

For a long time Europeans said he was the pilot who guided Vasco da Gama from Malindi to India in 1498. Most historians now doubt this; the pilot was probably a Gujarati or another Arab. In the Gulf he is honoured as the Lion of the Sea.
